title: UK MP Tanmanjeet Dhesi Urges Punjab Government to Resolve NRI Grievances
excerpt: The Labour MP and Defence Committee chair proposes direct flights between Amritsar and London and a one-window grievance system for overseas Indians facing property disputes and extortion calls.
body:
• UK Labour MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi has urged the Punjab government to establish a one-window grievance redressal system for NRIs facing property disputes, extortion calls, and bureaucratic hurdles.
  • Dhesi proposed a 'Punjab Fly Initiative' summit to push for direct flights between Amritsar and London, which he says would transform connectivity for the Punjabi diaspora in the UK.
  • The Slough MP, who chairs the UK House of Commons Defence Committee, met with Punjab NRI Affairs Minister Sanjeev Arora to discuss diaspora concerns.
  • Dhesi also called for reopening the Kartarpur Corridor for UK passport holders and raised the case of British Sikh Jagtar Singh Johal, detained in India since 2017.

Dhesi's Push for NRI Rights

Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, the UK Labour MP for Slough and chair of the House of Commons Defence Committee, has renewed his call for the Punjab government to address long-standing grievances faced by overseas Indians — particularly the Punjabi diaspora in the United Kingdom.

https://x.com/dailyajitnews/status/2088960414692651063

In a meeting with Punjab's NRI Affairs Minister Sanjeev Arora, Dhesi outlined a series of proposals aimed at making it easier for UK-based NRIs to navigate property disputes, land grab cases, and the persistent problem of extortion calls that target overseas Indians with assets in Punjab.

"NRIs contribute enormously to Punjab's economy through remittances and investment, but they face a maze of bureaucratic obstacles when trying to protect their property rights or resolve disputes," Dhesi said, according to ANI.

Direct Flights and Aviation Hub

Central to Dhesi's proposals is the 'Punjab Fly Initiative,' a summit concept that would bring together aviation stakeholders, government officials, and diaspora organisations to push for direct flights between Amritsar's Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport and London.

Currently, most UK-based Punjabis fly via Delhi or Mumbai to reach their home state, adding hours and cost to an already long journey. Dhesi argues that direct Amritsar-London flights would not only benefit the diaspora but also boost Punjab's tourism and business ecosystem.

"Direct flights between Amritsar and London would be transformative. The Punjabi diaspora in the UK is one of the largest in the world, and they deserve a direct connection to their homeland."

— Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, MP for Slough

Kartarpur Corridor and Johal Case

Dhesi also raised two sensitive diplomatic issues during his discussions. He called for the reopening of the Kartarpur Corridor to UK passport holders, allowing British Sikhs to visit the historic gurdwara across the India-Pakistan border without the restrictions that currently apply to non-Indian passport holders.

Additionally, Dhesi raised the case of Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh from Dumbarton, Scotland, who has been detained in India since November 2017. The case has been a recurring point of contention between the UK and Indian governments, with Dhesi and other British MPs calling for Johal's release or fair trial.

One-Window Grievance System

Perhaps the most practical of Dhesi's proposals is the one-window grievance system — a single point of contact for NRIs to file complaints, track cases, and receive updates on property disputes and other legal matters in Punjab. The current system, which requires NRIs to navigate multiple departments and often travel to India for court dates, has been a source of frustration for decades.

Punjab has attempted various NRI helplines and portals in the past, but none have achieved the streamlined efficiency that the diaspora demands. Dhesi's proposal draws on similar systems in other Indian states and in countries like the Philippines, which has dedicated overseas worker protection offices.

What's Next

Minister Arora reportedly assured Dhesi that the Punjab government would consider his proposals seriously. With state and local elections always on the horizon, NRI issues carry significant political weight in Punjab, where remittances from the UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East form a substantial part of the rural economy.
